item.title: Bereaved Brother: PA's terror lawyer just won a seat in Knesset
item.description: Hillel Fuld, brother of terror victim Ari Fuld, has accused Osama Saadi, a lawyer and member of the Joint List, of representing the Palestinian Authority in a lawsuit over its payments to the family of his brother’s killer.

item.title: US: Cost of war with Iran estimated at $47 billion, and could rise further
item.description: The cost of the war in Iran to the US military is estimated at $47 billion, CBS reported, based on an estimate by the US Central Command (CENTCOM). The amount does not include the costs of damage caused to US bases in the Middle East, so the total cost is expected to be higher.

item.title: Consul General Akunis calls for broad national unity government following elections
item.description: Israeli Consul General Ophir Akunis urges political leaders to form a broad unity government following the Knesset elections, stressing the importance of national unity for Israel, Diaspora Jewry, and the country's security.

item.title: EU congratulates Israel on its election
item.description: A Spokesperson for the European Union issued the following statement following yesterday's Knesset elections in Israel: "The European Union congratulates the Israeli people on yesterday’s elections, which saw a high voter turnout, reflecting Israel’s vibrant democracy. There now begins a period of political negotiations to form the next Israeli government. The EU looks forward to engaging with the next government on the basis of our longstanding relationship and commitment to democratic principles and common values, as well as to further advancing people-to-people contacts. The EU approach will continue to be based on a frank and open dialogue in view of advancing our bilateral cooperation, addressing all issues of concern and working together to promote regional stability, security, and a just and lasting peace."

item.title: UTJ overtakes Shas in partial election results
item.description: The change shows a shift in the balance of power among the haredi parties, with the UTJ party pulling ahead by tens of thousands of votes.

item.title: President calls for Compromise: "Come with an open mind"
item.description: President Isaac Herzog welcomed the high voter turnout, announced that consultations on forming a government would begin next week, and called on political parties to prevent another election.

item.title: Netanyahu warns against government with Arab parties
item.description: Netanyahu blasts Joint List after MK Osama Saadi accuses Israel of genocide and ethnic cleansing, warns 'bloc of change' seeking to form government with Arab parties.

item.title: From deputy minister to being outvoted by 'joke' candidate, Sharren Haskel's election Flop
item.description: Despite Jonathan Pollard's backing and an alliance with Aleh Yarok, Sharren Haskel's party receives just 804 votes, trailing two fringe parties.

item.title: 77.6% counted: Eisenkot and Bennett gain seats at expense of Joint List, Liberman
item.description: Partial official results updated at 12:32 p.m. with approximately 77.6% of the votes counted: Change bloc gains two seats since the previous update, rising to 49 seats. Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar rose to 22 seats, and Naftali Bennett's Together party rose to 12, while the Joint List dropped to 11 and Yisrael Beytenu dropped to seven.

item.title: 70% of the votes counted: Joint List gains a seat at the expense of Eisenkot
item.description: According to partial official results of Israel's 26th Knesset elections, updated at 10:50 a.m. on Wednesday, with approximately 70.7% of the votes counted, the coalition bloc remains at 54 seats, while the change bloc loses a seat, dropping to 47. The Joint List gained a seat from 12 to 13, at the expense of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party which has dropped to 20 seats. Ra'am remains at six seats.
